referents.why: Third masculine singular on the verb of cl1 (he called night). The nearest agreeing doer of the same naming in cl0 is God (w2). Elohim takes singular agreement with a singular verb, so the plural morph on the noun does not block it.
referents.category: implied subject carried over from prior clause

links.why: Order reversed. The calling of light and darkness (cl0, cl1) comes before the evening (cl2), so the builder direction runs backwards.
Plain waw opens cl1 and joins the two namings. No cause or result.
wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from cl1, which is not inside a speech.
wayyiqtol cl3 continues the narrative line from cl2.

none_fit.what: Name-giving: God called the light day and the darkness night. A naming is not a saying, so no content link fits, and no link type records giving a name.

cant_tell.what: cl4, day one, an appositional summary of the evening and morning (cl2, cl3)
cant_tell.why: The form does not settle whether it elaborates them or only closes the day. No link added.
